title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din (1137-1193) was an Ayyubid ruler of Egypt and Syria, active a century after El Cid's exile (1081-1094) and thousands of km away. The engine offers other options (a generic Saracen/Berber cavalry commander, an unnamed King or Castle-produced unit, or even a renamed hero), so this was fully avoidable.

37 CAMEL_RIDERs as the core of the Andalusian/Valencian army: taifa and even Almoravid forces in Iberia fought overwhelmingly as light horse (jinetes), Berber infantry and archers; camel cavalry was a Levantine/North African desert arm, not a Levante-Iberian one. AoE2 supports light cavalry, cavalry archers and spearmen that would have fit.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x18 plus desert-style dressing gives the map a Near Eastern/Saharan look; the Ebro valley and the Valencian huerta were irrigated farmland, orchards and Mediterranean scrub.

Enemy CAVALIER x11 (Feudal/Castle-era heavy Frankish-style knight upgrade) for the Muslim side sits oddly beside the camel spam; Muslim Iberian armies did not field the mailed Western lance charge as their mainstay.
TEMPLE_RUIN gaia object reads as a classical/pagan temple rather than an Iberian Roman or Visigothic remnant (ROMAN_RUINS and CASTLE_RUINS were the correct choices and are also present).

issues_found: SALADIN is placed as the enemy commander at Valencia: an Ayyubid sultan of Egypt/Syria who died in 1193, a century and a continent away from al-Qadir of Valencia or the Almoravid commanders El Cid actually faced. A renamed generic Saracen/Berber unit was the available and correct choice.

Player 2's army is 37 CAMEL_RIDER plus 11 CAVALIER — camel-heavy hosts are wrong for Andalusi/Almoravid warfare in the Levante, which fielded Berber and Andalusi light horse, jinetes and infantry; the engine's Light Cavalry/Cavalry Archer/Spearman mix was available.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture and unit sets are not assigned to Iberian/Saracen at all — an avoidable omission given Spanish and Saracen (or Berber) civs exist.
18 TREE_PALM_FOREST plus a TEMPLE_RUIN give a Near-Eastern desert dressing rather than the Ebro valley and Valencian huerta.
Alfonso VI, al-Mu'tamin of Zaragoza, al-Qadir of Valencia and Yusuf ibn Tashfin appear nowhere as placed objects; only El Cid himself is characterised.

The middle of the campaign is invented generic questing — an ambush, a traitor 'ally', a rescue mission — in place of documented episodes such as Almenar (1082), the capture of Berenguer Ramon II at Tevar (1090), or the twenty-month blockade of Valencia.

Defeat is triggered by the death of a generic KNIGHT ('key ally', presumably Minaya Alvar Fanez), who in fact outlived El Cid; and victory turns on slaying Saladin rather than on the surrender of Valencia.
Player 1's roster includes CHAMPION, CAVALIER and CROSSBOWMAN — a late-game imperial retinue rather than the small band of exiled Castilian knights and foot the brief promises to grow.

Player 2's commander is the SALADIN hero — an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of 12th-century Egypt/Syria, a century later and from an entirely different theatre than the Taifa/Almoravid lords of Zaragoza's rivals or Valencia. The engine offers generic Saracen/Berber units that could have been renamed 'al-Qadir', 'Ibn Jahhaf' or 'Berenguer Ramon II', so this was avoidable.

Both players' civilizations are set to RANDOM, so architecture, unit skins and tech tree may render as Britons, Japanese, Aztecs, etc.; Spanish for El Cid and Saracens/Berbers for the opposition were both available.

Enemy army is 37 Camel Riders out of ~61 units — camel cavalry was not the mainstay of Andalusi or Almoravid armies in Valencia; Berber light cavalry/knights and infantry would be far closer and are all in the engine.

The historical turning points are absent: no Almenar (1082), no capture of Berenguer Ramon II at Tevar (1090), no two-year blockade of Valencia (1093-94). Instead the middle acts are generic filler — an 'Ambush Leader', an unnamed 'Traitor', an 'Enemy Warlord' taunt, a rescue side-quest.
TREE_PALM_FOREST used as the dominant vegetation (18 objects) reads as a Saharan/Levantine desert rather than the Ebro valley and Valencian huerta.

Defeat condition on a generic KNIGHT labelled only 'Key Ally Dies' — Minaya Alvar Fanez is named in dialogue but the death condition is not identified with him, so it encodes an arbitrary unit-preservation rule.
Valencia is described as 'breached' and stormed; in fact El Cid took it after a long starvation blockade and a negotiated surrender in June 1094.
